title: Gemini 4 Carbon Pricing: Costs and Limits in 2026
summary: Gemini 4 carbon pricing spans free to $199.99 monthly, but the true cost depends on each tier's usage limits and which features you need.
body_markdown:
## Hidden costs and limits behind the overrun


Your bill is decided by rules the headline price leaves out: how much you can use before pricing changes, what gets metered separately, and what the vendor never writes down. Those gaps are where an uncapped account gets expensive.


> Your bill is decided by rules the headline price leaves out: how much you can use before pricing changes, what gets metered separately, and what the vendor never writes down.


### Usage and rate limits


Long prompts are the usual trap: past a certain length, many providers charge a higher rate on both what you send and what comes back. The page that shows the base price may not say where that line sits.


Rate limits, the ceiling on how fast you can send requests, are often unpublished or tied to an account's history. Your own limit shows up when requests start failing, usually during your busiest hour.


### Metered and add-on charges in Gemini 4 Carbon


When a feature sounds like part of the product, it's often billed on its own meter. Storing frequently reused prompts so they load faster can carry an hourly storage fee.


Web search built into a model is commonly charged per batch of queries, on top of the text you pay for. If an agent searches on every turn, that line can outgrow the model charge.


When the discount window closes, your bill rises with no change in your usage, so introductory pricing deserves the same suspicion. Put the end date in your calendar the day you sign up.


### Seat minimums, contract terms and region limits


With a seat minimum, you pay for a floor of users even if only a few log in. Annual terms lock in a commitment, so an overrun can't be fixed by cancelling mid-year.


Some features are offered only in certain regions, and moving workloads to a permitted one can change the rate or add a fee. These terms live in the order form or the docs, not on the pricing page.


Before you commit, ask the vendor in writing which limits are unpublished, which features carry their own meter, and when any introductory rate ends. A vendor who won't answer has told you something about what your first overrun will look like.
